extracted.intended_audience: school and college administrators, Title IX Coordinators, institutional legal counsel, and policymakers responsible for Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble discussion and final-rule explanations of recipients' obligations under revised Title IX regulations, focusing on definitions (e.g., student, actual knowledge), grievance process design (response vs investigation), supportive measures, reporting pathways, and related procedural clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'students' versus 'person/individual' language
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX and the final regulations use 'person' or 'individual' to ensure the non-discrimination mandate applies broadly to anyone in a recipient's education program or activity; where the final regulations use 'students' or 'students and employees' the terms are used not to narrow Title IX's reach but to require particular actions reasonably intended to benefit students, employees, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: §106.30 defines sexual harassment as conduct that deprives 'a person' of equal access and defines 'complainant' as an 'individual.' When the regulations intend to include 'applicants for admission' the phrase is used explicitly (e.g., §106.8(b)(2)(ii)). The use of 'students' should be interpreted as targeting recipients' obligations to benefit students rather than excluding others from Title IX protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'student' (34 CFR 106.2(r))
rubrics_metrics.description: The existing regulation defines 'student' as 'a person who has gained admission.' 'Admission' means selection for part-time, full-time, special, associate, transfer, exchange, or any other enrollment, membership, or matriculation in or at an education program or activity operated by a recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines suggestions to broaden 'student' to include persons not enrolled. This definition aligns with the 'formal complaint' definition in §106.30 requiring complainants to be participating in or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program when filing a formal complaint. An applicant who has been admitted is considered attempting to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality requirement for Title IX personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations require impartiality on the part of Title IX personnel (Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and persons who facilitate informal resolutions) to reinforce the truth-seeking purpose of a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality is reinforced by treating all parties with dignity, respect, and sensitivity without bias, prejudice, or stereotypes. The truth-seeking purpose underlies the grievance process; personnel must avoid partiality while engaging the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed approaches permitted but not equated with impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not equate 'trauma-informed' and 'impartial' in a manner that undermines the grievance process; nothing in the final regulations precludes recipients from applying trauma-informed techniques, practices, or approaches so long as they are consistent with §106.45(b)(1)(iii) and other requirements in §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While trauma-informed practices reflect best practices from research and clinical fields, recipients must ensure such practices do not conflict with impartiality or specific procedural requirements of grievance processes (e.g., fairness, opportunity to participate). Trauma-informed methods may be used as long as they comply with the procedural mandates in §106.45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of 'days' for regulatory timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not prescribe a specific method for calculating 'days' referenced in timeframes (e.g., ten 'days').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain flexibility to adopt whichever method works best operationally — calendar days, school days, business days, or a method already used by the recipient. The Department will not mandate a single calculation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to public and private recipients and constitutional cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations apply to all recipients covered by Title IX (those receiving Federal financial assistance), including public and private institutions. The Department recognizes that public recipients have constitutional obligations while private ones do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must follow fair, reliable procedures consistent with Title IX enforcement. Nothing in the final regulations requires recipients to restrict constitutional rights; the Department cannot and will not require private recipients to abide by constitutional restrictions that do not apply to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of recipient's obligation to respond to a report versus obligation to investigate a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations distinguish a recipient's obligation to respond to reports of sexual harassment (e.g., by offering supportive measures) from the recipient's affirmative obligation to investigate formal complaints under §106.45 (which may lead to disciplinary sanctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under §§106.44 and 106.45, recipients must offer supportive measures in response to a report irrespective of whether a formal complaint is filed; only filing or signing a formal complaint initiates the grievance process/investigation that may produce discipline. This separation aims to encourage reporting while allowing complainants greater control over whether an investigation occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures requirement irrespective of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer supportive measures to a complainant irrespective of whether the complainant files a formal complaint or the Title IX Coordinator signs a formal complaint initiating a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are individualized services listed non-exhaustively in the §106.30 definition of 'supportive measures.' The recipient must offer such measures promptly upon notice of allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation when supportive measures are not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient does not provide a complainant with supportive measures, the recipient must document the reasons why such a response was not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances under §106.45(b)(10)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should maintain records explaining why supportive measures were not offered or provided to allow review of whether the recipient's response was non-deliberately indifferent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies following a finding of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require a recipient to provide remedies to a complainant where a respondent has been found responsible; remedies may include individualized services non-exhaustively listed in the §106.30 definition of 'supportive measures.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to mandate prevention and community educational programming as required remedies or obligations, though such programming is permitted and may be appropriate as part of remedies depending on the facts. Whether prevention/education is an appropriate remedy is fact-specific for the recipient to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge triggers obligation to respond (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are liable for responding to every allegation of sexual harassment of which the recipient is aware (i.e., actual knowledge). Actual knowledge triggers prompt response obligations, including offering supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition of actual knowledge and its application ensure recipients cannot ignore known allegations for institutional self-interest. The final regulations revise the actual knowledge standard to ensure elementary and secondary students may report to any school employee and to respect complainant autonomy at postsecondary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge scope for elementary and secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: For elementary and secondary schools, the definition of actual knowledge is expanded to include notice to any employee of the school; any person (victim, witness, third party) may report and trigger the recipient's obligation to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expansion recognizes that young children do not distinguish among school adults and ensures prompt responses and offering of supportive measures upon notice to any school employee. The regulations do not alter other mandatory reporting obligations under Federal, State, or local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary institutions: universal mandatory reporting not imposed
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not impose a universal mandatory reporting system for postsecondary institutions; recipients retain the discretion to require employees to report to the Title IX Coordinator but are not required to do so by the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may choose to instruct all employees to report if they determine such a system best serves their population, but universal mandatory reporting can reduce confidential disclosure options and may chill reporting in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification obligations about reporting options and Title IX Coordinator contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify their educational community (students, employees, parents of elementary/secondary students, and others) of clear, accessible reporting options and of contact information for the Title IX Coordinator (office location, telephone number, email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must include how to report in person, by mail, telephone, email, or any method resulting in the Title IX Coordinator receiving the person's verbal or written report. Recipients bear the burden of ensuring the community can locate reporting channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'actual knowledge' includes notice of allegations — no requirement to await probable cause
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'actual knowledge' includes notice of allegations of sexual harassment; a recipient cannot wait to respond until it has probable cause that the sexual harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient's prompt response under revised §106.44(a) must include offering supportive measures irrespective of whether the complainant files or the Title IX Coordinator signs a formal complaint. ESSA or other obligations may inform a decision to sign a formal complaint in cases involving employees, but the obligation to offer supportive measures is triggered by notice of allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification: 'vicarious liability' replaces 'respondeat superior' in actual knowledge definition
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid confusion between the legal term 'respondeat superior' and the term 'respondent,' the Department revised the definition of 'actual knowledge' in §106.30 to use 'vicarious liability' instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Vicarious liability' more readily conveys the concept of being liable for the actions or omissions of another without causing unnecessary confusion with 'respondent.' The change is intended to improve clarity in the regulations' language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding when information is partial — obligation despite missing details
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient need not have received facts that definitively indicate whether the complainant's equal access has been effectively denied in order to be required to respond promptly in a non-deliberately indifferent manner; the 'complainant' is an individual alleged to be the victim of conduct that could constitute sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with partial information, the recipient must respond (including offering supportive measures) and may seek additional information as appropriate; the response obligation is triggered by allegations, not by conclusive proof that equal access was denied.
